correctness.rationale: For a 5-regular graph and total labels <=k, vertex weights range through 6,...,6k, giving k>=ceil((n+5)/6). Handshake forces even n; n<=10 permits only 6,8,10. At n6 the unique K6 has explicit two-label assignment with distinct weights 11,10,8,9,7,6. For n8 and n10, fixing vertex0 complement neighbors to {1..n-6} is w.l.o.g.; an independently written recursion over residual complement degrees with Erdős–Gallai pruning yields exactly 167 and 527481 labeled normalized completions. A SECOND independent program replayed the two source cert8 masks and ALL 149 source cert10 masks against EVERY completion, computing H=G∩F and constructing vertex labels by the same proved degree-class sufficient condition, checking actual weights: all 167 and all 527481 pass. The full 149-mask JSON was reconstructed byte-for-byte; Git blob SHA1 matches pinned e6fb480a1420419fa11715b5a83ac4824cd3d5c5, size 2431. This is genuinely exhaustive finite proof with a proved relabeling normalization, not sample enumeration.
